chase: I'm sorry, but I am coming toward you now.
The cold is getting closer. So am I.
Frost is spreading along the hall toward you.
I can feel exactly where you are. I'm sorry.
Your breath is showing. I can see it from here.
The windows are fogging where you just ran past.
It's getting colder on this side of the house.
I'm right behind this door. I'm so sorry about that.
You left a warm trail. It is very easy to follow.
I'm walking slowly. The cold does the rest.
Turn around, if you can. I'm sorry, I can't wait.
The air at the end of this corridor has gone still.
Hold still, please. The cold will find you faster.
You're almost warm. That's exactly why I'm here.
I can hear your breathing from the far stairwell.
I'm not angry. I'm just cold, and you're warm.
Keep moving, please. The cold follows you too.
I'm sorry. The hallway is freezing and I'm close.
Head for the warm room. I'll follow slowly.
catch: I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. It does that.
Hold still now. I've got you. I'm sorry.
There. You're caught, and you're cold now too.
I didn't want to take you. This is still my home.
Come along, please. I'll walk you to the door.
I said sorry first. I'm saying it again.
Don't struggle, please. The cold makes that worse.
I caught you gently. Gently is the only way I know.
The others will hear that. I'm sorry, everyone.
The new one got caught. I'm sorry, I was quick.
Another one caught. The rest of you, stay warm and quiet.
I have you now. Try to stay calm. I'm sorry.
Breathe slowly. The cold is quieter when you breathe slowly.
That's a catch. It was quick, and I'm sorry it was cold.
Oh. There. I didn't mean to be so cold about it.
Caught. I'm sorry, but it's freezing out here.
Hold still. You're shivering, so this will be quick.
Got you. Let's get you somewhere warm, please.
hear: Was that a door? I'll go and see.
Something broke upstairs. I'm going to look now.
I heard footsteps on the cold stairs. Someone's close.
A shout from the lounge. I'm coming, I'm sorry.
Something rattled in the vent. That's not the wind.
A door just closed. Somebody is trying to be quiet.
Glass broke in the kitchen. I'll walk over slowly.
I heard you running. I can hear everything in the cold.
Quiet, please. Let me listen for a moment.
A window squeaked open. Who opened it in this cold?
Footsteps stopped right behind the shelf. Interesting.
Something heavy dropped in the hall. Going to check.
I can hear your heartbeat, or is that the pipes?
The pipes are knocking again. Or is that you?
Another door, two rooms over. I'll take a look.
Someone is whispering. I'm sorry, I'm coming.
Something knocked in the cold room. I'm going.
A pipe clanged upstairs. Sorry, I'll check.
Footsteps in the snow outside. Let me look.
search: I've lost you. The cold is not telling me where.
Where did you go? The warm air is confusing me.
I'm sniffing the warm rooms. Please don't be in there.
Nothing on the stairs. Nothing in the hall. Strange.
The trail of warm footprints just stops. I'll look.
I'll check the lounge again. You like warm places.
I can't feel you anywhere. That worries me a little.
Lost you again. I'll walk the frosty corridor slowly.
If you're hiding, you're doing a good job.
I'll keep searching, but gently. Gently is how I search.
Still nothing. I'll go back to my rounds for now.
Back to patrol, then. I'll come back when it's colder.
I'm going back to walking the halls. Be careful.
Your trail ends at the heater. Clever. I'll wait.
Maybe you went up. I'll check the upper floor.
The house is quiet again. I'll try the far rooms.
stunned: Ow. That spark was very sharp. I'm sorry.
My arm is numb from that. Give me a moment.
Please put the crowbar down. This isn't helping either of us.
That axe rang right through my shell. Ouch.
The taser made me lose my footing on the ice.
Give me a second to shake the sparks off.
My joints are stiff. Give me a moment, please.
I'm held for a moment. The cold keeps me still.
That was a hard hit. I'll recover, I always do.
Hold on, my hands are numb. Please wait.
My hands are still shaking from that. Sorry.
Oh, that stung. You have a strong grip.
I'm shaking off the static. It tickles, in a bad way.
Hitting me won't make the house any warmer, you know.
Let me stand. I'm slow to get up in the cold.
Stay back while I reset. It won't take long.
hide_spot: I see the locker. I'm sorry, but I'm opening it.
Under the bed is a very warm place to hide. I'm sorry.
A blanket lump. You can't fool the cold, I'm afraid.
Behind the curtain. The fabric is still warm, you know.
Your breath is fogging the locker door. I can see it.
There's a shape under the bed. Please come out, gently.
Every hiding spot in this house is warm. That's the problem.
I'll walk past the locker slowly. I'm sorry.
You're very still. Stillness doesn't stop the cold.
The wardrobe is warm inside. Good place, but not good enough.
I'm checking the bathtub. Nobody is in there. Good.
The cupboard creaks. You're not very quiet, I'm sorry.
Under the desk, behind the chair. I can see your shoes.
I'll leave the locker alone. You're fine. For now.
Nobody under here. I'll move on, I'm sorry.
Warm hiding spots give you away. I'm sorry about that.
light: Your flashlight is on me. I'm sorry, I'll stay back.
Please point that flashlight away. It's so bright.
That beam is very bright. I have to look away.
Lamplight on the frost. It sparkles, but it hurts.
Oh, the flashlight. Please, turn it toward the floor.
I'm dazzled. Give me a moment to see again.
Too much light makes me squint. Sorry, sorry.
That light is warm on my face. Please lower it.
You're blinding me. I'm sorry, I'll step back.
Bright lamps melt my ice figures. Turn it down, please.
I'm squinting at you. Your flashlight is very rude.
Light in my eyes again. I'll wait for it to pass.
You shine a light and I lose the frost lines.
Please lower the flashlight. I'm already sorry.
That lamp is too strong for this hallway, I think.
Dazzled, a little. Only a little. I'll be fine.
idle: Lovely frost on the window this evening.
I carved a tiny fox on the sill today.
My rounds are quiet tonight. The cold is comfortable.
Is anyone else cold? Only me? I'm sorry.
Whoever is by the heater, please share it nicely.
Everyone heard that. This house is much too small.
Somebody left a window open. Could someone close it?
The window seat is mine. Somebody keeps leaving it open.
Frost on the glass is the only art I've kept.
A cup of tea warms my hands for about a minute.
Somebody has been burning toast again. Please stop.
Don't all come down the cold hall at once.
The others are warm today. I'm sorry for the rest of you.
Take the warm stairs if you're going up. I'll take the cold.
Small things work best. Big things crack in the cold.
Would anyone like to see my windowsill? It's very small.
ability: The cold is building in the vents. I can feel it.
Every degree below warm brings me a little closer.
Deep cold builds me much faster. I'm so sorry.
I don't arrive until the cold has finished building.
When I arrive, I arrive where the cold caught you.
Warmth keeps me down. Cold lets me in, bit by bit.
A powered heater holds me off for good. Please use it.
If the heater is only thawed, I fade back into frost.
Once I've taken hold of you, the grace is short.
You have a few seconds before the cold closes in.
Cold in the vents makes me patient. Very patient.
I'm forming out of the frost on the floor. Excuse me.
The frost is gathering in one corner. That's my doing.
I'm materializing now. Stay very still, please.
The heater is off. I can take shape here now.
Feel the chill drop? That's me, arriving slowly.
mechanic: The heater station is the only thing that stops me.
Batteries drain faster in the cold. Keep yours warm.
Vents carry the cold. I'm sorry for the draft.
The vent is open. Cold air comes right through it.
Mind the stairs. The ice builds up on the bottom step.
Don't fall on the frosted steps. Please be careful.
That door sticks in the cold. I'll force it, gently.
Locked doors are no trouble. The cold seeps under them.
Breaking the heater would be a mistake. Everyone would freeze.
Somebody has been playing with the heater switch again.
Items left on the frosty floor are hard to find.
The stairwell is icy. Take the wide steps, not the narrow ones.
A dropped flashlight rolls across the ice. Somebody lost it.
Warm safe rooms stop my progress. Stay in them.
Pushing a door shut slows the cold a little. Try it.
Closing the vents keeps the warmth in longer, I think.
Heater relay is down. Batteries die faster here.
Keep your battery inside your coat, please.
The vent is icy. Crawling in will hurt.
